label: 720XP-48Y6
description: Arista CCS-720XP-48Y6 - 1RU Cognitive Campus leaf: 48x 10M/100M/1G RJ45 PoE+ (Ethernet1-48) plus 6x 1/10/25G SFP (Ethernet49-54).

poe.note: Arista's own row for CCS-720XP-48Y6: "PoE Power Budget Single / Dual PSU 982 W / 1850 W" (supported supply PWR-1021-AC, 68 W / 93 W typical / maximum excluding PoE). The switch ships with one 1050 W supply, so 982 W is the figure recorded here and the 1850 W two-supply ceiling is noted rather than used. Per port the datasheet caps the copper group at 30 W (802.3af/at), which is what the 48 template ports declare.

notes: Vendor rows read 2026-11-20. Arista CCS-720XP data sheet "https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/CCS-720XP-Datasheet.pdf": "720XP-48Y6 - 48 x 10M-1GbE RJ45 @ 30W - Uplinks: 6x 25G", with the series described as "Managed 802.3af/at/bt power services ... up to 90W per RJ45 port" (90 W is the 48TXH-2C-S mGig port, not this one). Ordering information names "CCS-720XP-48Y6-F ... 48 x 10/100M-1G PoE, 6 x 25G SFP switch, front to rear air, 1 x 1050W AC". Arista 720XP/722XPM 1RU quick start guide "https://www.arista.com/en/qsg-720xp-series-1ru/720xp-series-1ru-overview" prints the budget row quoted in `poe.note`. The six uplinks are SFP28 cages (25G SFP in the vendor's table), so they source no power; only Ethernet1-48 are PSE ports. This spec used to describe PoE+ in prose while declaring no `poe-pse` capability and no budget, so the box powered nothing and `show power inline` answered that no port on it could supply power.
